newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian drug chief resigns to study at Harvard.
newsitem.headline: Colombian drug chief resigns to study at Harvard.

text.p: Colombia's anti-drugs chief announced his resignation on Monday and said he was moving to the United States -- a country his office has often criticised in the past.

Joaquin Polo, head of the National Drug Policy office, announced his departure in an interview with local radio in which he strongly denied the move was prompted by reported budget problems or differences with other government officials.
"My resignation is due to strictly personal reasons," he told the Radionet news programme.

Polo became head of the Drug Policy office just over a year ago and he used the post to lobby for closer worldwide cooperation in the fight against drugs. He had called, specifically, for stronger action from developed countries like the United States to clamp down on runaway drug use.
Polo said he had been granted an Organisation of American States-backed scholarship to study at Harvard University. He did not elaborate.
Government officials could not be reached for immediate comment on who President Ernesto Samper might name to replace Polo.

Polo's resignation comes at a time when recent government moves to lift Colombia's six-year-old ban on the extradition of drug traffickers and other criminals have raised widespread fears of a possible violent backlash by drug gangs.
He did not comment on the extradition issue in his brief radio interview or say whether he had received death threats as the visible head of anti-drug policy in Colombia.
